slides.texte_overlay:
Things a man should never
apologise for
Taking time for himself. An evening alone, a long run, a quiet Sunday. Recharging isn't selfish. A rested man shows up better for everyone around him.
Saying no to things that drain him. A party he doesn't want to go to, a favour he can't afford. A calm, polite no is a sign of self-respect, not rudeness.
Having feelings. Being sad after a loss, nervous before a big day, moved by a film. Feeling things deeply is human, and hiding it only makes everything heavier.
Asking for help. With work, with money, with his mind. Strong men ask when they need to. Pretending you can handle everything alone is what breaks people.
Wanting to keep learning. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and I've stopped apologising for being the curious one in every conversation.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. I've stopped apologising for being the curious one in the room.

slides.texte_overlay: Leaving situations that disrespect him. A job that belittles him, a friend who mocks him, a date that turns rude. Walking away calmly is a skill, not a failure.
Growing and changing. New habits, new interests, a new way of thinking. People who knew the old you might be surprised. That's fine. Growth is the whole point.
